Interface IuOidcPrincipal

All Superinterfaces:
Principal
All Known Implementing Classes:
OidcPrincipal
public interface IuOidcPrincipal extends Principal
Client application view of principal user identity established via interaction with an OIDC provider.

The OpenID Connect claims associated with the principal are available through getOidcClaims().

  • Method Details

    • getOidcClaims

      default IuOidcClaims getOidcClaims()
      Gets the OpenID Connect claims associated with this principal.

      The default view resolves every standard claim through getClaim(String, Class). Implementations may override this method to return a richer claim view.

      Returns:
      claims associated with this principal

    • getAcr

      default String getAcr()
      Gets the authentication context class this principal's authentication satisfied.

      Its absence is the claim

      OpenID Connect §2 leaves acr values to agreement between the parties using them; IU's provider writes the authenticating authority's unique identifier — a federated SAML identity provider's entity ID, where a deployment authenticates that way.

      Nothing constrains a client_id from reading like a principal name, so Principal.getName() alone does not say whether a token answers for an end user or for a client (RFC 9700 §4.15). This does: a token whose subject authenticated names who authenticated them, and one that answers for the client itself has no such authority to name. Three readings cover every token a provider issues — this claim present is an end user; absent with getActor() is a delegation, where the authority belongs to the actor and is read through IuOidcActor.getAcr(); absent with no actor is the client itself.

      Declared here rather than on IuOidcClaims, which states what a claims source may assert about an end user. This describes the authentication instead, and a provider writes it from what it established rather than asking a source for it.

      Returns:
      acr claim; null when this principal's subject did not itself authenticate
      See Also:
      • OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §2

    • getActor

      default IuOidcActor getActor()
      Gets the claims describing the actor a delegated token names, when somebody is acting for this principal.

      RFC 8693 §4.1 puts the acting party's identity in the act claim and confines that object to claims about the actor alone, so what comes back here describes whoever obtained the token — never the subject it answers for. A relying party reads it to show its user whose session they are looking through, and reads IuOidcActor.getAcr() to learn who authenticated them.

      Null is the ordinary case. Most tokens are not delegated, and answering an empty claims view would make "nobody is acting" read the same as "somebody is acting and this token says nothing about them".

      Returns:
      claims describing the actor; null when this token is not delegated
      See Also:
      • RFC 8693 §4.1

    • hasScope

      default boolean hasScope(String... scope)
      Determines whether a scope was granted to this principal.

      An implementation checks the space-delimited scope claim from the token it verified: an ID token for a client principal, or an access token for an API bearer principal. Scope names are case-sensitive.

      Parameters:
      scope - scopes to check for
      Returns:
      true if the claim includes at least one requested scope; else false

    • hasScope

      default boolean hasScope(Iterable<String> scope)
      Determines whether a scope was granted to this principal.

      An implementation checks the space-delimited scope claim from the token it verified: an ID token for a client principal, or an access token for an API bearer principal. Scope names are case-sensitive.

      The default denies every scope, so a principal implementation predating this method compiles and answers deny-by-default rather than failing with AbstractMethodError; override it to check an actual claim.

      Parameters:
      scope - scopes to check for
      Returns:
      true if the claim includes at least one requested scope; else false

    • hasRole

      default boolean hasRole(String... role)
      Determines whether this principal has an asserted role.

      An implementation checks the roles claim from the token it verified: an ID token for a client principal, or an access token for an API bearer principal. Role names compare without regard to case.

      Parameters:
      role - roles to check for
      Returns:
      true if the claim includes at least one requested role; else false

    • getAuthorizationDetails

      <T extends IuAuthorizationDetails> Iterable<T> getAuthorizationDetails(Class<T> detailInterface, String type)
      Gets the authorization details released by the authorization server.

      The token response's authorization_details value is authoritative when present, including when it is empty. When the response omits that value, this method reads the matching entries from the verified ID token.

      Type Parameters:
      T - authorization details interface type
      Parameters:
      detailInterface - authorization details interface class used to decode matching entries
      type - authorization_details type property value to match
      Returns:
      released authorization details matching type

    • getAccessToken

      String getAccessToken(URI resourceUri) throws IOException
      Gets an access token issued to this principal for use with a given remote resource.

      May require an on-behalf-of exchange with the OpenID Provider's token endpoint.

      Parameters:
      resourceUri - root resource URI for the API to get an access token for
      Returns:
      access token for use at the indicated resource URI
      Throws:
      IOException - if communication with an upstream provider is interrupted
